If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment remains neutral (0.33–0.67) across 7+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias in late horizon (16–30 days) to account for mean reversion.

If sentiment peaks >0.80 in last 3 days and forecast is below historical 30-day mean, add 1–2% upward adjustment in mid-horizon to capture sentiment-driven breakout.

If sentiment is volatile (±0.33 or more in 3 consecutive days), apply 0.5–1.0% smoothing adjustment across all horizons to dampen overfitting.
